en.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) directed Ziyād ibn Abīh, his appointed governor of Fārs, to avoid the administrative burden of collecting land tax (kharāj) prematurely, a practice that often led to exploitation before the harvest was secured. This instruction underscores the Shia emphasis on justice (ʿadl) in economic governance, ensuring that fiscal policies do not impose undue hardship on the populace. The prohibition reflects a broader principle of fairness in state administration, where the ruler acts as a trustee rather than a mere collector of revenue.

isnad_matn.matn_ar: كَلَامٍ طَوِيلٍ كَانَ بَيْنَهُمَا، نَهَاهُ فِيهِ عَنْ تَقَدُّمِ الْخَرَاجِ:

narrators.name_ar: ٤٧٦. وقال (عليه ‏السلام) لزياد ابن أبيه. وقد استخلفه لعبد الله بن العباس على فارس وأعمالها،
